text:
alex: Deploy bot flagged image publish from ci-release as SKIPPED — provenance mismatch for sha256:abc123... I saw the push to ECR failed verification. Anyone on call?

deploy-bot: [automated] publish attempt 1792345678 by ci-release:SKIP_PROVENANCE
reason: provenance signature missing or identity mismatch
ecr registry: 123456789012.dkr.ecr.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/redwood/serve:2026-03-19-57
observed manifest digest: sha256:abc123...
expected builder id: ci-builder-7 -> got: unknown
suggested action: hold, do not retag until investigation

jason: copying logs, attaching gist -> https://gist.github.com/xxxx
looks like cosign verification failed: "no matching signature"

priya: @jason can you paste the cosign verify output? also which base image was used? :thinking:

jason: cosign verify --key kms://projects/... 123456789012.dkr.ecr...@sha256:abc123
output:
```
Verification for sha256:abc123 failed: no signatures found
```

liam: could be parallel publish that skipped signing. we had a retry loop in buildkite that forks images. maybe a race where signed artifact pushed to gcr and a subsequent retag pushed unsigned to ecr.

maya: If that's the case we should avoid retagging published digest. options:
- force re-run CI with explicit SIGN step
- pin deployments to previous good digest and roll forward after signed image
- open short change window for emergency sign-and-publish with release-eng present

ops-bot: suggest emergency policy: if provenance missing -> block release and pin k8s deploy to last-known-good-digest. automatic rollback allowed for <=5% traffic with canary. manual approval required for re-publish.

sara: from playbook: to pin deploys run:
```
kubectl set image deploy/serve serve=123456789012.dkr.ecr.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/redwood/serve@sha256:prevgood
kubectl rollout status deploy/serve
```
also update release-notes/rollout with "image pin due to provenance verification failure"

priya: I'll coordinate a re-run of the build with enforced cosign key and add a pre-publish verify step. ETA ~25m.

alex: ok create a release note stub and add to #release-notes
I'll hold the change window — don't promote any tags until we confirm signatures. :lock:

jason: one more datapoint: gcr stored the signed manifest at sha256:def456; ecr attempt used retag to sha256:abc123 which lacks sbom. how did retag end up changing digest? maybe we used 'docker tag' and pushed which creates new manifest.

liam: yep docker tag + push will create new manifest and if you don't re-sign the resulting manifest it won't have provenance. that's on the build pipeline.

maya: action items:
- priya re-run CI with sign step (in progress)
- jason confirm which digests are signed (done)
- ops pin k8s to prevgood (liam)
- alex notify release managers and lock change window

alex: adding list to this thread so release managers see it: @sara @maya @liam

deploy-bot: publish blocked, label=provenance-missing, ticket created: #INC-4521

sara: noted. I'll add a short blurb to release notes and hold the scheduled canary for 2 hours. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

priya: CI re-run succeeded and cosign signature now present for sha256:ghi789
new push created digest sha256:ghi789 signed by ci-builder-7

ops-bot: recommend promoting signed digest ghi789 -> stable tag redwood/serve:stable and then gradual canary

alex: agreed. liam, coordinate rollout and confirm metrics for 30m canary, then full promote.

liam: on it. starting canary now.

jason: adding postmortem note: root cause = retag-without-sign from ephemeral helper pipeline. will add gating for publish that enforces sign-step. short-term fix: prevent direct 'docker tag/push' in release step.

maya: closing loop: update runbook and PR for pipeline change -> https://github.com/redwood-inference/release/pull/412

alex: thanks everyone. keep this thread for final deploy status.

liam: canary OK at 30m, no errors. promoting to 100%.

alex: closing thread — resolved. :white_check_mark:
